[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on cyclic AMP as an intracellular messenger and on the cells that depend on it. Two calcium/calmodulin-stimulated adenylate cyclases, ADCY1 and ADCY8, generate cAMP in neurons in response to calcium entry, coupling synaptic activity to kinase signalling and long-term potentiation; the serotonin receptor HTR6 and a G protein gamma subunit sit upstream of the same second-messenger route, while CAMK2N1 restrains calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II and so tunes the calcium arm of the response.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on stress-activated transcriptional signalling and its supporting membrane and metabolic machinery. Its recognisable core is the kinase TAK1 (MAP3K7) acting upstream of the CREB/ATF family factors ATF1 and ATF2, a route by which cytokine, TGF-beta and stress inputs are converted into changes in gene expression governing inflammation, survival and differentiation; loss of TAK1 signalling causes inflammatory and developmental failure.
